items.passage: I was fourteen the summer the stream below our house dried to a bed of gray stones, and my father, who had poled visitors across it for twenty years, had nothing left to ferry. That August a boy named Marcus, staying with an aunt up the road, challenged me, Nalani, to race across the riverbed and back. He mentioned, while we stretched, that his parents were splitting up and that he was flying home to Ohio on Sunday to learn which of them he would live with. I knew every loose stone on that crossing. Halfway back, I let my foot find the wobbly one I always stepped over, and I stumbled just long enough. Marcus whooped at the far bank. My father, watching from the porch, only lifted his coffee cup. That fall the rains returned and filled the channel to its old banks.

items.passage: Clay still drying on your wrists, you came down to the Lyon studio that morning in 1919, Elodie, to find Marcel already at the wheel, his army coat folded on the stool. items.passage: When the hives were opened yesterday, Senhor Bruno, my brother stood at the edge of the yard with your Latin grammar under his arm, unopened, as it has been since the evening you left our house. I therefore enclose a jar of this season's honey and ask that you resume his lessons on Monday next, at the usual hour. My father has agreed to stay in town on those days. I was the newest hand, and the day before I had hidden a crooked spine of mine beneath the press, sure no one had seen. Konrad, the foreman, had seen; he only raised an eyebrow and said nothing. Overnight the rain had washed the soil from the yard and uncovered a rotted crate full of bindings, each one lopsided, each stamped with the small anchor Konrad had used as an apprentice. He lifted the worst of them, wiped it on his apron, and set it in my hands beside my own. Colette, he said, and nothing more. ### lit40-medium-02-067 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation

I was fourteen the summer the stream below our house dried to a bed of gray stones, and my father, who had poled visitors across it for twenty years, had nothing left to ferry. That August a boy named Marcus, staying with an aunt up the road, challenged me, Nalani, to race across the riverbed and back. He mentioned, while we stretched, that his parents were splitting up and that he was flying home to Ohio on Sunday to learn which of them he would live with. I knew every loose stone on that crossing. Halfway back, I let my foot find the wobbly one I always stepped over, and I stumbled just long enough. Marcus whooped at the far bank. [질문] Based on the text, why does the narrator most likely stumble during the race?
A) She is suddenly frightened by the loose stones on the unfamiliar crossing.

C) She hopes that losing will convince Marcus to stay on the island longer.
D) She wants to give Marcus a small victory before he faces a hard change.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
경주 전에 Marcus는 부모의 이혼과 일요일에 집으로 돌아가야 한다는 사정을 털어놓는다. 이어 화자는 건널목의 돌을 모두 알고 있으면서도 늘 피하던 흔들리는 돌을 일부러 밟는다. 두 단서를 연결하면 힘든 변화를 앞둔 Marcus에게 작은 승리를 주려 했음을 알 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문과 다른 감정, C는 결과를 동기로 착각한 것이며, B는 지문에 없는 원인이다.

### lit40-medium-02-086 — skill inferences · 유형 symbolism
[지문]
When Zofia climbed to the roof that last evening in Thessaloniki, her father was already kneeling beside the water tank, a tin of sealant open at his knee. For eleven summers the tank had wept a thin rust-colored line down the wall, and for eleven summers he had said he would fix it next week. Eda, from the next roof, used to joke that the stain was older than Zofia's English. Zofia had stopped noticing it, the way she had stopped noticing that he never asked about the school prize ceremony he had missed. Now he pressed the sealant into the seam with his thumb and said, in Greek, that he should have done this long ago. She answered in English that it was fine, though her suitcase was already packed downstairs. Below them, the harbor lights came on and a ferry horn sounded twice.

[질문] In the text, the leaking water tank most likely represents
A) the father's pride in his practical skills, which Zofia has never truly valued
B) the family's lack of money, which has kept them from making needed repairs
C) a long-neglected hurt that her father tries to mend only as she is leaving
D) the language gap between father and daughter, which neither one can bridge

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
물탱크는 11년 동안 새면서도 '다음 주'로 미뤄졌고, Zofia가 그 얼룩을 잊은 방식은 아버지가 놓친 시상식을 잊은 방식과 겹쳐 서술된다. 아버지는 딸이 떠나는 날에야 틈을 메우며 진작 했어야 했다고 말하고, 딸의 가방은 이미 싸여 있다. 따라서 탱크는 너무 늦게 다뤄지는 오래된 상처를 상징하므로 C가 정답이다. D는 언어 차이가 언급되어 그럴듯하지만 반복된 수리 지연과 사과의 맥락을 설명하지 못하고, A와 B는 근거가 없다.
